title: Fabrication of Micro-tissues using Modules of Collagen Gel Containing Cells
protocol: Cut 2 to 3 m lengths of polyethylene tubing (0.76 mm I.D. x 1.22 mm O.D.).
Thread a 20 G1 needle into one end of the tubing.
Coil the tubing and place in a self-seal pouch (7 1/2" x 13").
Place the two ends of the tubing at the unsealed end of the bag and tape them with gas sterilization tape.
Seal the bag and perform gas sterilization.
Add 128 μL of 10x α-MEM per mL of collagen to a tube containing the necessary amount of collagen for the desired length of tubing, then mix by repeatedly pipetting.
Neutralize the collagen by adding sodium bicarbonate until the solution has a pH of 7.4 (it should turn light pink).
Keep neutralized collagen on ice until ready to use.
Embed cells at a concentration between 1 million and 20 million cells per mL in the required medium, if applicable.
Remove media from cells and wash with 5 mL PBS.
Remove PBS and add 3 mL trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate the cells in trypsin-EDTA for 5 min at 37°C.
Resuspend cells in 7 mL media.
Count cells.
Transfer the required number of cells for embedding to a 15 mL conical tube.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate media off the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in the neutralized collagen and keep on ice.
Cut off the sealed end of the bag containing the polyethylene tubing.
Attach a 3 ml syringe to the 20G needle in one end of the tubing using sterilized tweezers.
Insert the other end of the tubing into the neutralized collagen until the tip is at the bottom of the conical tube using sterilized tweezers.
Pull the collagen into the polyethylene tubing by retracting the plunger of the syringe slowly.
Remove the 20G needle from the tubing and put both ends back into the bag.
Tape the bag shut.
Incubate the bag at 37°C for 60 min.
Flip the bag over every 15 min if collagen contains cells.
Autoclave headers and blade for the cutting device and tray to hold tubing.
Assemble the cutting device.
Place tubing in a sterile tray in front of cutting device.
Load tubing into the cutting device.
Set up a 50 mL conical tube containing 25 mL of media at the outlet of the cutting device to collect cut modules.
Cut tubing to lengths of 2 mm using the cutting device.
Incubate cut modules at 37°C for 60 min in the 50 mL conical tube.
Vortex 50 mL conical tube containing modules in the tubing for 10 sec.
Let modules settle to the bottom of the tube for about 5 min.
Transfer settled modules to a 15 mL conical tube using a wide mouth 10 mL serological pipette.
Repeat steps from vortexing to transferring twice more.
Settle modules into the bottom of a 15 mL conical tube with 5 mL of media for the embedded cells.
Remove media from endothelial cells and wash with 5 mL PBS.
Remove PBS and add 3 mL trypsin-EDTA to the endothelial cells.
Incubate the cells in trypsin-EDTA for 5 min at 37°C.
Resuspend cells in 7 mL media.
Count cells.
Pellet cells at 300 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend pelleted cells in 5 mL endothelial cell media.
Add 5 mL of the media containing endothelial cells to the modules.
Incubate modules statically by inverting and setting upright at 37°C for 15 min. Repeat.
Dynamically seed endothelial cells by gently rocking the tube at 37°C for 60 min.
Repeat static incubation twice.
Place the modules in a non-tissue culture treated plate and incubate overnight at 37°C.
The next day, place the modules in a new non-tissue culture treated plate with fresh media (50:50 mix if using co-culture system) to remove unattached endothelial cells.
Incubate modules coated with endothelial cells until they cover 100% of the surface. This usually takes about 7 days.
